INCIDENT REPORT - <LOCATION> - <DATE>

<Filed the same day, by someone who was there. Same-day reports are worse
than considered ones, because the writer has not yet worked out how to
phrase it.>

SUMMARY

<What happened, in one flat paragraph. Do not describe suffering. Describe
the outcome and the hour.>

SEQUENCE

    <HHMM>    <Event.>
    <HHMM>    <Event.>
    <HHMM>    <Event.>

CONDITION OF <THE ROOM / THE EQUIPMENT / THE SITE>

<Everything worked. Say so plainly. The equipment is not the failure.>

WHAT THIS MEANS

<Two facts that cannot both be true. State both. Do not resolve them —
have the writer admit, on the page, that they cannot write the sentence
that reconciles them.>

PERSONNEL

<Who was present. Then a sentence about what was reported, phrased so a
careful reader notices that reported and true are different words.>

ACTION TAKEN

<An order. Then, if it suits, the time it was issued and the reason it
arrived too late to matter.>
